subject: Subprocessor chain, UK addendum coverage, and limited-scope TIA for pilot
thread_content:
From: Laura Mitchell <laura.mitchell@medicore.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Harris <tom@proceedlaw.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on subprocessor chain & jurisdictional assertions

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. As we scope the pilot (EU residents only for now) Legal asked for clarity on a few things before we proceed:

1) Can you provide a current subprocessor map that includes (a) vendor name, (b) country of processing, and (c) role (storage/compute/logging)? We need this to confirm whether any downstream processors are located in jurisdictions outside the EEA/UK.

2) If Redwood uses multi-hop processors (e.g., an EU vendor that onboards a US-based analytics provider), how do you handle the contractual flowdown and SCC coverage? Are you able to provide an attestation that all onward transfers relevant to our data are covered by SCCs or the UK IDTA/UK Addendum?

3) For a limited pilot we want to exclude backups or analytics results from being copied to US-operated secondary systems. Can Redwood make an operational carveout or scoping exclusion in the TIA/DTIA for that pilot?

Attached: processor_map_request.pdf (short template our privacy team uses).

Could you loop in the right people on your side and let me know when we can get the map and a proposed approach?

Best,
Laura Mitchell
Senior Privacy Counsel, Medicore Health
laura.mitchell@medicore.com

----------

Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -0700

Hi Laura — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Marissa (acct exec) so we can get you a concise pack.

Proposed next steps:
- Kimberly: confirm contractual position re: multi-hop/subprocessor chaining and whether we can provide a signed attestation.
- We produce redacted subprocessor map (vendor + country + role).
- Draft a limited-scope TIA/DTIA for your pilot excluding US backups/analytics, and flag any operational constraints.

Would Monday or Tuesday next week for a 30-min call to run through the map and scoping?

Thanks,
Jonas
Director, Customer Security & Compliance (on behalf of Redwood Inference)
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Mitchell <laura.mitchell@medicore.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on subprocessor chain & jurisdictional assertions

Hi Laura — appreciate the attachment and the concise asks. High-level answers below, followed by what we will deliver and timelines.

Quick overview:
- Subprocessor map: we will provide a redacted CSV listing vendor name, primary processing location(s), and role. For vendors that themselves subcontract, we include the level of subcontracting ("onward: yes/no") where known.
- Multi-hop/onward transfers: our approach is contractual + technical. Contractually, Redwood requires subprocessors to flow down data protection obligations (SCCs or equivalent clauses where applicable) and to notify us of their own subprocessors. For onward transfers from an EU-based vendor to a third country, Redwood either (a) ensures the vendor has SCCs in place with that vendor's subprocessors or (b) we perform a TIA that documents technical and organizational safeguards.
- UK coverage: where processing includes UK personal data, we apply the UK Addendum/IDTA in addition to the standard EU SCCs, and we can provide a UK-specific attestation if required.

What we will produce within 5 business days:
1) Redacted subprocessor_map_20270316.csv (vendor, country, role, onward flag).
2) SCC_implementation_note.pdf — a 2-page summary describing how SCCs are implemented in our supply chain and where we rely on technical safeguards (encryption at rest/in-transit, access controls, logging retention).
3) Draft limited-scope TIA scoping sheet (TIA_scoping_template.xlsx) tailored for your pilot that documents the specific processing activities to exclude (backups/analytics export to US) and the operational controls to enforce the carveout.

Attestation and signatures:
- We can provide a signed attestation confirming that, for the listed vendors and for the scope of the pilot, either SCCs/IDTA flowdown is in place or Redwood has onboarded the vendor following our conditional safeguards process. We will supply this via DocuSign (link below) after your team reviews the map.

Operational note:
- One caveat: some third-party analytics or telemetry providers host aggregated telemetry in the US as part of their service. For the pilot exclusion you requested, we can configure telemetry exports to be disabled and provide logs demonstrating those exports are blocked. However, full eliminations (e.g., vendor-managed backups stored in a US region) may require either vendor-side config or a contractual restriction that might impact that vendor’s SLA. We will flag any vendors for which full exclusion is not operationally feasible.

Related attachments (will send): subprocessor_map_20270316.csv, SCC_implementation_note.pdf
DocuSign attestation link (will be active once map is approved): https://app.docusign.com/attest/REDWOOD-ATTEST-2027
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0BREDWOOD/subprocessor-evidence

Let us know if you want a low-latency call to walk through the map or if written responses are preferred.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Kim/Team — this is very helpful, thanks. A couple follow-ups:

- We will review the redacted map, but can you also flag any vendors where full exclusion (no backups to US) is not feasible? That will help our product team decide whether to widen the pilot geography.
- For the TIA scope: can you include a short draft DPA clause we can present internally that documents the operational carveout ("Redwood shall ensure that no backups or analytics exports containing Medicore personal data are stored or processed in US-operated secondary cloud regions for the pilot period")? We can then scope that into our purchase order.

I attached a brief pilot_scope.xlsx we use to indicate data classes and retention requirements.

If everything looks good, we can sign the attestation once redwood returns the map.

Best,
Laura
